sentences.en: Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun.
sentences.zh: 启发人心、富有挑战、令人振奋、妙趣横生。

sentences.en: These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers.
sentences.zh: 《自然》杂志的读者在一系列关于艺术家与研究人员合作的报道中，用这些词语来描述他们参与艺术与科学合作的体验。

sentences.en: Nearly 40% of the roughly 350 people who responded to an accompanying poll said they had collaborated with artists; and almost all said they would consider doing so in future.
sentences.zh: 在参与配套民意调查的约350人中，近40%的人表示曾与艺术家合作过；几乎所有受访者都表示未来会考虑这样做。

sentences.en: Such an encouraging result is not surprising.
sentences.zh: 这样令人鼓舞的结果并不令人意外。

sentences.en: Scientists are increasingly seeking out visual artists to help them communicate their work to new audiences.
sentences.zh: 科学家们越来越多地寻求与视觉艺术家合作，帮助他们向新的受众传播自己的研究成果。

sentences.en: “Artists help scientists reach a broader audience and make emotional connections that enhance learning.”
sentences.zh: “艺术家能帮助科学家接触到更广泛的受众，并建立起能够促进学习的感情共鸣。”

sentences.en: One respondent said.
sentences.zh: 一位受访者说。

sentences.en: One example of how artists and scientists have together rocked the senses came last month when the Sydney Symphony Orchestra performed a reworked version of Antonio Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons.
sentences.zh: 上个月，悉尼交响乐团演奏了安东尼奥·维瓦尔第《四季》的改编版，这便是艺术家与科学家共同震撼感官的一个例子。

sentences.en: They reimagined the 300-year-old score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season—provided by Monash University’s Climate Change Communication Research Hub.
sentences.zh: 他们对这首拥有300年历史的乐曲进行了重新演绎，注入了由莫纳什大学气候变化传播研究中心提供的每个季节的最新气候预测数据。

sentences.en: The performance was a creative call to action ahead of November’s United Nations Climate Change Conference in Glasgow, UK.
sentences.zh: 这场演出是在英国格拉斯哥联合国气候变化大会召开之前发出的一次富有创意的行动呼吁。

sentences.en: But a genuine partnership must be a two-way street.
sentences.zh: 但真正的合作必须是双向的。

sentences.en: Fewer artists than scientists responded to the Nature poll; however, several respondents noted that artists do not simply assist scientists with their communication requirements.
sentences.zh: 参加《自然》杂志调查的艺术家比科学家少；然而，多位受访者指出，艺术家并不是简单地帮助科学家满足其传播需求。

sentences.en: Nor should their work be considered only as an object of study.
sentences.zh: 他们的作品也不应仅仅被视为研究的对象。

sentences.en: The alliances are most valuable when scientists and artists have a shared stake in a project, are able to jointly design it and can critique each other’s work.
sentences.zh: 当科学家和艺术家在一个项目中拥有共同的利益、能够共同设计项目并彼此评价对方的工作时，这种合作最有价值。

sentences.en: Such an approach can both prompt new research as well as result in powerful art.
sentences.zh: 这种方法既能促进新的研究，也能产生震撼人心的艺术作品。

sentences.en: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) to explore the role of technology in culture.
sentences.zh: 半个多世纪前，麻省理工学院成立了高级视觉研究中心，以探索技术在社会文化中的作用。

sentences.en: The founders deliberately focused their projects around light—hence the “visual studies” in the name.
sentences.zh: 创立者们刻意将项目围绕“光”展开——这正是名称中“视觉研究”的由来。

sentences.en: Light was a something that both artists and scientists had an interest in, and therefore could form the basis of collaboration.
sentences.zh: 光既是艺术家也是科学家感兴趣的东西，因此可以成为合作的基础。

sentences.en: As science and technology progressed, and divided into more sub-disciplines, the centre was simultaneously looking to a time when leading researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 随着科学技术的进步并分化为更多的分支学科，该中心同时也在展望这样一个时代：顶尖的研究人员也可以成为艺术家、作家和诗人，反之亦然。

sentences.en: Nature’s poll findings suggest that this trend is as strong as ever, but, to make a collaboration work, both sides need to invest time, and embrace surprise and challenge.
sentences.zh: 《自然》杂志的调查结果表明，这一趋势依然强劲，但要想合作成功，双方都需要投入时间，并欣然接受惊喜与挑战。

sentences.en: The reach of art-science tie-ups need to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication, and participants must not fall into the trap of stereotyping each other.
sentences.zh: 艺术与科学的合作不能仅仅停留在研究传播这一必要目的上，参与者切不可陷入彼此刻板印象的误区。

sentences.en: Artists and scientists alike are immersed in discovery and invention, and challenge and critique are core to both, too.
sentences.zh: 艺术家和科学家都沉浸于发现与创造之中，而挑战与批判对两者而言也都是核心所在。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, art-science collaborations have ______.
questions.analysis: 首段《自然》读者用“启迪、挑战、激发、有趣”等词描述艺术-科学合作体验，且近 40% 受访者表示与艺术家合作过，多数人愿意尝试，即获得积极反响。

questions.stem: The reworked version of The Four Seasons is mentioned to show that ______.

options.A: art can offer audiences easy access to science
options.B: science can help with the expression of emotions
options.C: public participation in science has a promising future
options.D: art is effective in facilitating scientific innovations

questions.analysis: 第三段以悉尼交响乐团重编维瓦尔第《四季》为例：把最新气候预测数据注入古老乐曲，在气候大会前以创作呼吁行动，说明艺术能让观众轻松接触科学。

questions.stem: Some artists seem to worry about in the art-science partnership ______.
questions.analysis: 第四段提到受访者指出“艺术家并非只是协助科学家做传播”，其作品也不应仅被当作研究对象，暗示部分艺术家担心自身作用被低估。

questions.stem: What does the author say about CAVS?

options.A: It was headed alternately by artists and scientists.
options.C: Its projects aimed at advancing visual studies.
options.D: Its founders sought to raise the status of artists.

questions.analysis: 第五段介绍 MIT 的 CAVS 中心：围绕光这一艺术家与科学家共同兴趣开展项目，成为富有价值的艺术-科学联盟典范。

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author holds that art-science collaborations ______.

options.A: are likely to go beyond public expectations
options.C: should do more than communicating science
options.D: are becoming more popular than before

questions.analysis: 末段强调艺术-科学合作“需超越研究传播这一必要目的”（need to go beyond the necessary purpose of research communication），即应不止于传播科学。
